title: Fix cross-tenant ARP leakage and DNS cache staleness during peering failovers
creator: Daniel Kim
description: Summary: Multiple Dedicated customers reported intermittent cross-tenant traffic and name-resolution failures during VPC peering disruptions and failovers. Impact: some tenants saw short-lived connection handoffs where ACKs/ARP entries were accepted across tenant veth namespaces; DNS lookups returned stale answers from local node caches after peering flaps, causing request routing to land on decommissioned endpoints. Root cause hypothesis: a combination of (1) delayed cleanup of kernel-level ARP entries when the network agent accelerated pod/ENI churn, and (2) our local dnsmasq cache not being invalidated on route table/peering rebind events. Reproduction: stress test with controlled peering failover (simulate route withdrawal + rapid reattach) using perf harness in /infra/tests/peering-failover. Observed: transient ARP entries for deleted tenant interfaces for 10-45s and negative TTLs in node-local DNS cache. Current mitigation: emergency iptables rule to drop cross-namespace ARP packets on affected clusters + TTL-rewrite in dnsmasq for dedicated nodes (rolled to 3 customers). Long-term fix: implement proactive ARP/neighbor flush in the network agent on peering events, and hook route-change events to dnsmasq cache purge (or switch to per-tenant DNS cache with eviction on peering events). The fix includes kernel neighbor table management, network-agent changes, and an operator-level rollout plan with canaries and guarded fallbacks.
comments: 2026-03-10 — Customer support (CS-5432) opened escalation: AcornHealth reported 2 incidents in the last 24h where requests were routed to wrong tenant backend during maintenance window.
2026-03-11 — Initial triage: Reproduced ARP leakage locally with peering-failover harness. Attached pcap+trace to ticket. (link: https://drive.redwood/example/ENG-25642/pcap)

2026-03-12 — Hotfix deployed to cluster us-west-2-dedicated-a: iptables rule dropped cross-namespace ARP; reduced customer impact. Rollback-safe. (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/net-agent/pull/1421)
2026-03-13 — Network-agent prototype: added neighbor table flush on PeeringDown/PeeringUp events. Running canary against 5% of nodes. Logs: https://logs.redwood/example/peering-canary

2026-03-14 — Found correlated issue where dnsmasq retained cache entries for deleted route prefixes. Added dns purge hook in agent (branch: dns-peering-purge). Observability dashboard created: /console/dashboards/dedicated/peering-arp-dns
Next steps: finish kernel neighbor-table patch, integrate dns purge, smoke test on staging, coordinate with SRE for canary windows and customer comms.
postmortem_notes: 1) Add automated e2e test in CI: simulate peering flaps and assert no cross-namespace ARP entries within 5s
2) Improve observability: emit neighbor-table-change metrics and per-node dns-cache hit/miss with peering context
3) Operator tooling: one-click invalidate-node-dns-cache and neighbor-flush for escalations
4) Update runbooks and notify Dedicated accounts of upcoming fix and mitigation steps
